stops.title: Applications of Gauss' law
stops.inShort: Gauss' law: Φ = ∮ E·dA = q_enclosed / ε₀. Used to find E due to a uniformly charged sphere (E = q/(4πε₀r²)), infinitely long straight wire (E = λ/(2πε₀r)), and infinite plane sheet (E = σ/(2ε₀)).

stops.title: Electric potential, potential energy & equipotential surfaces
stops.inShort: Potential V = W/q₀ = q/(4πε₀r). Electric dipole potential V = p cos θ / (4πε₀r²). Equipotential surfaces have constant V, are perpendicular to E, and never intersect.
sections: 8.4 Potential due to Point Charge & Dipole

stops.title: Conductors, dielectrics & electric polarization
stops.inShort: Inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium, E = 0 and V is constant. Polar dielectrics have permanent dipole moments; non-polar do not. Polarization P = χ_e ε₀ E.

stops.title: Capacitors, combinations & energy stored
stops.inShort: Parallel plate capacitor C = ε₀ A / d (with dielectric k: C = k ε₀ A / d). Series: 1/C_s = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂; Parallel: C_p = C₁ + C₂. Energy stored U = ½ C V² = ½ Q²/C = ½ Q V.

stops.title: Displacement current & Van de Graaff generator
stops.inShort: Displacement current I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt maintains continuity of current across a capacitor. Van de Graaff generator produces very high electrostatic potential (several MV) using corona discharge and hollow conductor shell.

items.f: E_wire = λ/(2πε₀r),  E_sheet = σ/(2ε₀),  E_conductor = σ/ε₀

items.s: On axis θ = 0°; on equator θ = 90° ⇒ V = 0.

items.f: C = k ε₀ A / d,  U = (1/2) C V²

board.text: Electric potential 'V' at a distance 'r' from a point charge is directly proportional to ____.
Calculate the electric field intensity at a point just near the surface of a charged plane sheet, measured from its mid-point. [σ = 8.85 μC/m², ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/N·m²]
Obtain an expression for equivalent capacitance of two capacitors C₁ and C₂ connected in series.
board.answer:
In series combination, charge Q on each capacitor is the same, while total potential difference V = V₁ + V₂.
V₁ = Q/C₁, V₂ = Q/C₂, and V = Q/C_s.
Thus Q/C_s = Q/C₁ + Q/C₂ ⇒ 1/C_s = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂, or C_s = C₁C₂ / (C₁ + C₂).

points.text: Same charge Q and V = V₁ + V₂

board.text: Derive an expression for the energy stored in a charged capacitor.
board.answer:
Let a capacitor of capacitance C be charged to charge Q. At an intermediate stage with charge q, potential v = q/C.
Work done to add small charge dq: dW = v dq = (q/C) dq.
Total work W = ∫(0 to Q) (q/C) dq = Q² / (2C).
Since Q = CV, energy stored U = ½ Q²/C = ½ C V² = ½ Q V.

points.text: U = ½ Q²/C = ½ C V² = ½ Q V
